title: Inconsistency for objects returned by get_rest_info
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable, 4.6.2.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX A2000 12GB (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9651) - AMD Ryzen 7 7700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Attempting to use get_rest_info to get the nearest node in a cone facing away from the player camera. Shape query uses camera transform and is generated procedurally.  When using get_rest_info(), returned object will sometimes be nodes further away from origin than other colliding objects. There's nothing I've been able to find about what "nearest" collision means in this instance, so I'm assuming it means to the origin of the shape query

### Steps to reproduce

Generate a convex shape cone. Code I used to do so:
```gdscript
func generate_cone_cast(radius : float, height : float, segments : int = 16) -> ConvexPolygonShape3D:
	var output = ConvexPolygonShape3D.new()
	var new_points = PackedVector3Array()
	new_points.append(Vector3.ZERO)
	for i in segments:
		var angle = ( i* 2 * PI)/segments
		var point_x = radius * cos(angle)
		var point_y = radius * sin(angle)
		var point = Vector3(point_x,point_y,-height)
		new_points.append(point)
	output.points = new_points
	return output
```

Use convex shapes here:
`var output = physics_state.get_rest_info(shape_query)`
